title: Published npm package (library)
appliesWhen: A JavaScript or TypeScript package published to the npm registry for others to install, public or under a scope.
ask: Will this be published to npm for others to install? Public or scoped/private, ESM only or ESM and CommonJS, and does it ship TypeScript types?

sources.title: npm Docs: Trusted publishing for npm packages

guidance: Set "type" explicitly and define "exports" for every public entry point; in each condition object put "types" first and "default" last (Node.js packages docs, enforced by publint).
Adding or narrowing "exports" in an existing package is a breaking change: consumers lose every subpath not listed. Ship it in a major version, or export every previously used path.
Use a "files" allowlist (for example ["dist"]); package.json, README, LICENSE and the main file are always included. Never rely on .npmignore alone: a new secret file at the root ships by default.
Inspect the tarball with npm pack --dry-run before each release; source maps, tests, fixtures and .env files are the usual surprises.

ESM-only packages: Are The Types Wrong reports "ESM (dynamic import only)" for CommonJS consumers and exits 1; record ESM-only in the architecture and run attw with --profile esm-only. Dual ESM/CJS packages risk loading two copies (instanceof and singleton state break).

Publish from CI with trusted publishing (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD or CircleCI on cloud runners, npm CLI 11.5.1+ and Node 22.14+). Provenance is generated automatically on GitHub/GitLab for public repos and packages; repository.url must match the repository exactly.
After trusted publishing works, set Publishing access to "Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens", and delete old automation tokens.
A published version can never be republished with different contents; fix mistakes with a new patch version and npm deprecate, not by unpublishing.
Keep runtime dependencies minimal and pinned to compatible ranges; peerDependencies for frameworks the host app provides (React, etc.).

gates.title: package.json has the publishing fields
gates.command: node -e "const p=require('./package.json');const miss=['name','version','license','repository','files','engines'].filter((k)=>!p[k]);if(!p.exports&&!p.main)miss.push('exports or main');if(p.private)miss.push('private is true');if(miss.length){console.error('package.json needs: '+miss.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log(p.name+'@'+p.version+': publishing fields present')"
gates.architecture: Record the package name (scope), licence (SPDX), repository URL, entry points ("exports", plus "main"/"types" for older tooling), the "files" allowlist and the supported Node range in "engines".
acceptance: package.json has name, version, license (SPDX id), repository, exports or main, files and engines

gates.title: publint reports no errors or warnings
gates.architecture: Record the module format (ESM only, or ESM and CommonJS) and how the build produces each entry point listed in "exports".
acceptance: Every path in exports, main, module, types and bin exists in the packed tarball

gates.title: Types resolve for every supported module resolution (Are The Types Wrong)
gates.architecture: Record whether the package ships types (bundled .d.ts or generated) and which consumers it supports: node16 ESM and CJS, bundlers, node10. For an ESM-only package change the command to add --profile esm-only; for an untyped JavaScript package remove the gate with a reason.
acceptance: attw --pack . exits 0 for the chosen profile
No "Masquerading as CJS/ESM", "Resolution failed" or "No types" problems for supported resolutions

gates.title: The tarball contains only intended files and no secrets
gates.command: npm pack --dry-run --json | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',(d)=>s+=d).on('end',()=>{const files=JSON.parse(s.slice(s.search(/^\[/m)))[0].files.map((f)=>f.path);const bad=files.filter((f)=>/(^|\/)(\.env(\..+)?|\.npmrc|id_(rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519)|[^/]*\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)|credentials[^/]*)$/i.test(f));console.log(files.length+' files: '+files.join(', '));if(bad.length){console.error('remove from the package: '+bad.join(', '));process.exit(1)}})"
gates.architecture: Record the files allowlist and the build step that runs before packing (prepack or a CI build step).
acceptance: npm pack --dry-run lists only the built output, README, LICENSE and package.json (plus any documented extras)
No .env, .npmrc, private key, certificate or credentials file is in the tarball

gates.title: Versioning follows SemVer with a changelog
gates.architecture: Record what the public API is (the "exports" entry points and their types), how versions are bumped (manual, changesets, release-please) and where the changelog lives.
acceptance: Each release has a changelog entry naming breaking changes, features and fixes
Removing or changing an export, a type, the "exports" map, "engines" or the module format is released as a major version

gates.title: Releases are published from CI with trusted publishing, provenance and 2FA
gates.architecture: Record the release workflow (trigger, CI provider, id-token: write permission, npm CLI version), the trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com, dist-tags, and the account protection (2FA, tokens disallowed).
acceptance: The package is published from a CI workflow configured as a trusted publisher, not from a developer machine
The npm package page shows provenance for the latest version (public GitHub/GitLab repositories)
Every maintainer account has 2FA; package publishing access requires 2FA and disallows tokens

gates.title: Package licence and dependency licence compatibility need review
gates.architecture: Record the chosen licence and list the runtime dependencies (dependencies and bundled code) with their licences.
